correctness.rationale: Every step is exact and unrestricted: M^13=I+3B; the state period lifts because Bv is nonzero mod 3; the complete 8-row coefficient table identifies all mod-3 roots; six regular branches each have a nonzero unit lifting slope (one class at every higher power); Perrin residue 0 dies at mod 9; the exceptional Padovan residue 9 is divisible by 9 and its normalized function has precisely two simple roots mod 3, with f(t+3^m)-f(t)=3^m t mod 3^(m+1). Those roots each have three representatives at the original modulus, giving six exceptional classes. A separate pure-integer checker recomputed matrix coefficients, C_m congruences and complete periods through k=10.

originality.rationale: The claim is a new exact zero-frequency classification (4,6,9 versus 4,3,3) and special six-class mechanism, not the known order 13*3^(k-1). A full-text reading of Bravo (2023), publisher abstracts for Bravo et al. (2022) and Bravo-Irmak (2024), inspected OEIS A000931/A001608/A104217, focused web literature queries, an actual semantic mathematical-record search, and accessible own-claim comparisons identified no covering theorem. The 2022 full article remained inaccessible and earlier implicit general valuation results cannot be excluded; these are specific originality risks, not assertions of proven global priority.

value.rationale: The natural arithmetic invariant is the exact frequency of 3^k-divisible recurrence terms, not an arbitrary sampled segment. It refines known modular period tables to exact zero densities across infinitely many moduli, exposes a genuine 9-versus-3 dichotomy between two canonical Padovan-type sequences, and explains the extra six Padovan roots via a nonregular 3-adic branch. The proof supplies an explicit reusable lifting mechanism rather than a table extension.
